definition: An influence that can set an object in motion, slow it down, change its direction, or change its shape.
Done when a force moves an object a distance in the direction of the force – calculated as force times distance. Just holding something still does not count as work, even if it strains your muscles.
The unit of work and energy (J). Equal to 1 newton-metre (1 J = 1 Nm) – the amount of work needed when a force of 1 newton moves something 1 metre.
The ability to do work – can be thought of as stored work. Something that has energy can, in turn, make something else move, heat up, or glow. Measured in joules (J).
One of the different forms energy can take, e.g. potential, kinetic, chemical, electrical, heat, radiant and nuclear energy. Energy is converted between these forms.
Energy an object has because of its height. The higher up and the heavier the object, the more of this energy is stored in it.
Energy an object has because it is moving. The greater the speed and the greater the mass, the more of this energy is stored in it.
A common term for potential energy and kinetic energy. The two can be converted into each other, e.g. on a roller coaster.
Energy stored in substances, for example in food, fuel and batteries.
The energy in warm substances, held in the motion of their molecules. Produced as a by-product in almost all energy conversions.

namn_native: The principle of conservation of energy
definition: Energy can neither be created nor destroyed – it can only be converted between different forms. The total amount of energy is always conserved.
A series of energy conversions one after another, e.g. potential energy → kinetic energy → electrical energy → light and heat. Such a series always ends in heat eventually.
How much work or energy is done per second – calculated as work divided by time. The unit is watt (W).
The unit of power (W). Equal to 1 joule per second (1 W = 1 J/s). A hairdryer rated at 1000 W converts 1000 joules every second.
An older unit of power that James Watt introduced to compare the strength of a steam engine with that of draught horses. Equal to about 736 W.
How large a proportion of the energy supplied becomes useful energy, usually given as a percentage. The rest becomes heat. No machine reaches 100 %.
Aids such as the lever, the inclined plane and the pulley. They help us save force, but never work.
What you gain in force, you lose in distance. A tool can reduce the force needed, but then the object must be moved a longer distance.
A simple machine – a sloping surface that lets you roll or drag something up using less force, though over a longer distance.
A unit of energy (kWh) used on electricity bills. 1 kWh = 1000 watt-hours = a power of 1000 W maintained for 1 hour.
A natural resource from which we obtain energy. Divided into renewable (sun, wind, water, biofuel, geothermal energy) and non-renewable (coal, oil, natural gas, nuclear energy).
An energy source that does not run out, e.g. sun, wind, water, biofuel and geothermal energy.
An energy source that exists in a limited amount and will one day run out: coal, oil, natural gas and nuclear energy. Coal, oil and gas are fossil fuels.
A facility where an energy source is converted into electrical energy. In a hydroelectric plant, for example, the kinetic energy of falling water drives a turbine connected to a generator.
